title: The Safety, Pharmacokinetics, and Antiviral Activity of ABI ‐4334, A Novel Next‐Generation Hepatitis B Capsid Assembly Modulator

analysis.research_question_and_background: A novel, well‐tolerated, short‐term therapeutic for chronic hepatitis B virus infection (cHBV) is needed, as current treatments have limitations.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Two Phase 1 studies were conducted: Study 101 involved healthy volunteers with four single‐ascending dose cohorts and two once‐daily multiple‐ascending dose cohorts, while Study 102 involved participants with cHBV randomized 8:2 (ABI‐4334 [2 dose cohorts]:placebo). Overall, 54 healthy volunteers and 20 participants with cHBV were included in Studies 101 and 102, respectively.
analysis.methods: The safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of ABI‐4334 were examined in two Phase 1 studies. In Study 101, a placebo‐controlled design with single‐ and multiple‐ascending dose cohorts was used, and in Study 102, a randomized, blinded, placebo‐controlled design was implemented.
analysis.main_results: HBV DNA declines were observed in both HBeAg‐positive (n = 3) and ‐negative (n = 13) participants across doses. Additionally, reductions in pgRNA were noted in participants with detectable pgRNA at baseline.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that ABI‐4334 is well tolerated and demonstrate antiviral activity in participants with cHBV, supporting its development as a monotherapy or component of combination regimens.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide important insights into the potential of ABI‐4334 as a new therapeutic option for managing chronic hepatitis B virus infection, which could inform future clinical trials and treatment strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The studies were Phase 1 trials with limited sample sizes, which may restrict the generalizability of the findings. However, the evidence is strong given the consistent pharmacokinetic profiles and antiviral activity observed.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the safety, tolerability, and antiviral activity of ABI-4334, a novel capsid assembly modulator targeting HBV core protein, in two Phase 1 trials. Study 101 involved healthy volunteers with single- and multiple-ascending dose cohorts, while Study 102 included participants with chronic HBV infection randomized 8:2 (ABI-4334:placebo). ABI-4334 was well tolerated, with no serious adverse events reported. These findings support its continued development as a monotherapy or combination treatment for chronic HBV. The evidence is strong, but the limited sample sizes and Phase 1 design may affect generalizability.

title: Hepatitis B and D: Interferon-Based Therapy-For Clinical Trials or Standard of Care-Back to the Future?

analysis.scope_and_question: Interferon (IFN) has historically played a major role in chronic viral hepatitis B and D management over the last three decades.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: Widening utilisation of nucleoside/nucleotide analogues (NUCs) for hepatitis B viral suppression, which have a better side-effect profile, alongside the recent licensing of bulevirtide for treatment of hepatitis D, means that its clinical use has further declined.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Pegylated-interferon alpha (peg-IFNα) treatment is suboptimal with poor tolerability and achieves durable clearance of hepatitis B and D in only a limited number of patients.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Nevertheless, its use in hepatitis B has significantly increased the number of patients achieving hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) loss compared to those on NUCs alone.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Evidence has shown that peg-IFNα is also associated with overall improved long-term clinical outcomes in chronic hepatitis D, even for the many whose hepatitis D viral load rebounds after discontinuation.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines the historical and current role of interferon-based therapy in managing hepatitis B and D. It highlights the decline in clinical use due to the availability of nucleoside/nucleotide analogues (NUCs) and bulevirtide, which offer better side-effect profiles. Pegylated-interferon alpha (peg-IFNα) is noted as suboptimal with poor tolerability and limited durable clearance rates. However, its use in hepatitis B has increased HBsAg loss compared to NUCs alone. Additionally, peg-IFNα is associated with improved long-term clinical outcomes in chronic hepatitis D, despite viral load rebounds post-treatment. The review focuses on recent research advances and the potential for peg-IFNα to still play an important role in treatment strategies.

analysis.methods: Descriptive statistics summarized KAP levels, and associations between sociodemographic variables and KAP outcomes were examined using chi-square tests and logistic regression. The study used a structured questionnaire to collect data.
analysis.main_results: Although 98.0% of students had heard of HBV, 63.0% demonstrated good knowledge, while 37.0% had poor knowledge. analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design, which cannot establish causality. However, the evidence is strong due to the use of statistical analyses and a representative sample of high school students in a hyperendemic setting.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study from Mogadishu, Somalia, aimed to assess knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) related to hepatitis B virus (HBV) among high school students. The study's findings highlight the importance of improving adolescent HBV prevention in a hyperendemic setting. The evidence is moderate due to the cross-sectional design, which limits causal inference.

title: Fusion of segmental right-lobe IVIM-DWI metrics and GPR for non-invasive assessment of chronic hepatitis B–related hepatic fibrosis: a pilot study

analysis.research_question_and_background: A segmental intravoxel incoherent motion diffusion-weighted imaging (IVIM-DWI)/gamma-glutamyl transpeptidase-to-platelet ratio (GPR) fusion model was evaluated for the non-invasive assessment of chronic hepatitis B (CHB) fibrosis (controls vs. advanced) and compared with the aspartate aminotransferase-to-platelet ratio index (APRI) and Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4).
analysis.study_design_and_population: This retrospective study included 139 participants: 42 healthy controls (HCs), 46 with early hepatic fibrosis (EHF), and 51 with advanced hepatic fibrosis (AHF).
analysis.methods: IVIM-DWI parameters (apparent diffusion coefficient, slow diffusion component, fast diffusion component, and perfusion fraction) were extracted from segmental analysis of the right hepatic lobe (segments V-VIII). The GPR, APRI, and FIB-4 were calculated from laboratory values. The IVIM + GPR fusion model was developed using logistic regression. Model performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis with bootstrap internal validation.
analysis.main_results: EHF, FIB-4 achieved the highest area under the curve [AUC; 0.911, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.844-0.969) followed by APRI (0.843, 95% CI: 0.755-0.923). The IVIM + GPR fusion model (AUC = 0.745, 95% CI: 0.643-0.847) outperformed IVIM alone (AUC = 0.652) and GPR alone (AUC = 0.730) but did not outperform APRI or FIB-4. For AHF, the IVIM + GPR fusion model (AUC = 0.698) was comparable to APRI (0.573) and FIB-4 (0.637), with no significant differences among methods.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The IVIM + GPR fusion model may provide supplementary, opportunistic information during abdominal MRI or when serum markers are confounded by extrahepatic factors, but it should remain complementary pending validation in larger cohorts.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The fusion model should be considered, at most, a supplementary, opportunistic adjunct during abdominal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) rather than a replacement for FIB-4/APRI. FIB-4 and APRI remain first-line where laboratory panels are available.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: In the absence of a biopsy-proven S0 CHB group, HCs vs. EHF discriminates between HCs and established fibrosis rather than detecting incident fibrosis. The supplied evidence does not report the exact number of participants with confirmed HBV infection.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated a segmental IVIM-DWI/GPR fusion model for non-invasive assessment of chronic hepatitis B fibrosis, comparing it with APRI and FIB-4. The model showed improved performance over IVIM and GPR alone but was not superior to APRI or FIB-4 in distinguishing healthy controls from early fibrosis. For advanced fibrosis, the fusion model was comparable to APRI and FIB-4. The authors concluded that the fusion model may offer supplementary information during abdominal MRI or when serum markers are affected by extrahepatic factors, but it should not replace FIB-4 or APRI. The study's limitations include the absence of a biopsy-proven S0 CHB group, which restricts the model's ability to detect incident fibrosis. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the study's retrospective design and limited sample size.

title: Anti-Viral Treatment Eligibility and Treatment Uptake Among People With Chronic Hepatitis B in Australia: The REACH-B Study.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Treatment indication for chronic hepatitis B (CHB) varies across clinical guidelines. This study aimed to evaluate treatment eligibility and uptake in a large Australian cohort of people with CHB.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The REACH-B study recruited people with CHB managed through a national network of healthcare services. Participants were categorised into three groups: (1) receiving antiviral therapy; (2) untreated despite eligibility; (3) untreated and ineligible. Among 3648 participants (56% male; median age 48 years; 49% born in North-East or South-East Asia; 27% First Nations Australians), 14% were HBeAg positive and 7% had cirrhosis.
analysis.methods: Treatment eligibility was determined using Australian Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) criteria, and by international clinical guidelines.
analysis.main_results: Overall, 47% (n = 1666) were on antiviral therapy, 45% (n = 1573) were untreated and ineligible and 7% (n = 251) were untreated despite eligibility based on Australian PBS criteria.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: In adjusted analysis, the likelihood of remaining untreated despite eligibility was higher among women (aOR 1.59, 95% CI 1.34, 1.88) and younger participants (age 41-60 vs. > 60 years: aOR 1.51, 95% CI 1.01-2.28; ≤ 40 vs. 41-60 years: aOR 1.85, 95% CI 1.34-2.56). The proportion untreated despite eligibility increased to 13% when applying 2024 World Health Organisation guidelines and ranged 2%-44% based on other guidelines, highlighting the variability across the guidelines.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the variability in treatment eligibility criteria across guidelines and underscore the importance of monitoring treatment patterns as guidelines evolve. Lower treatment uptake among women and younger people despite eligibility partly reflects lower threshold for elevated ALT in women, and clinician determination of non-CHB related ALT elevation.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on self-reported data and potential biases in clinician determination of non-CHB related ALT elevation. The evidence is moderate as it is based on observational data and does not include experimental or longitudinal follow-up.

analysis.summary_en: This study, the REACH-B Study, evaluated treatment eligibility and uptake among people with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) in Australia. It found that 47% of participants were on antiviral therapy, while 7% were untreated despite eligibility based on Australian PBS criteria. The proportion untreated despite eligibility varied significantly depending on the guidelines used, ranging from 2% to 44%. The study identified that women and younger participants were more likely to remain untreated despite eligibility. These findings highlight the variability in treatment criteria across guidelines and the importance of monitoring treatment patterns as guidelines evolve. The study's evidence is moderate due to its observational nature and potential biases in clinician assessments.

title: Triple burden at the HIV–hepatitis B–malaria interface: viral–parasite interactions, epidemiological complexity and the case for integrated surveillance and community-based prevention in sub-Saharan Africa

analysis.scope_and_question: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, genotypes and disease. The review focuses on biological interactions, epidemiological complexity, and the case for integrated surveillance and community-based prevention in sub-Saharan Africa, particularly at the HIV–HBV–malaria interface.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This critical narrative review examines the evidence for biological interaction at each interface, the diagnostic and epidemiological traps that their overlap creates, and the case for integrated surveillance and community prevention. The review is based on a comprehensive analysis of existing literature and does not report specific study counts or meta-analysis methods.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: HIV-associated immunosuppression consistently increases the frequency and severity of malaria, and acute malaria transiently raises plasma HIV RNA. HIV also accelerates the natural history of chronic HBV. Antiretroviral and antimalarial drugs interact in clinically relevant ways.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: A direct interaction between HBV and Plasmodium is plausible, but it rests mainly on animal models and small, inconsistent human studies. No reliable estimate of triple infection exists. Fever, anaemia and abnormal liver tests during malaria can mask a concurrent chronic viral infection, and routine facility data can produce apparent coinfection patterns that reflect testing intensity rather than biology.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Integration should rest on shared delivery, not on assumed shared pathogenesis, and prospective cohorts and implementation trials are needed to show whether it improves outcomes and equity. Drawing on the World Health Organization’s guidance on integrated disease surveillance and response, a detect–verify–act approach is described that links community signals, confirmatory testing and confidential longitudinal records, while each infection keeps its own indicators and review cycle.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the complex interactions between HIV, hepatitis B virus (HBV) and malaria in sub-Saharan Africa, emphasizing the biological and epidemiological challenges they create. It highlights that HIV-associated immunosuppression increases malaria severity and that HIV accelerates HBV progression. Antiretroviral and antimalarial drugs also interact clinically. However, the evidence for direct HBV–Plasmodium interaction is limited to animal models and small human studies, with no reliable estimate of triple infections. The review advocates for integrated surveillance and community-based prevention strategies, suggesting a detect–verify–act framework. It calls for prospective studies to evaluate the effectiveness of integration in improving outcomes and equity.

title: Realizing personalized prediction for the reversal of chronic hepatitis B-associated liver fibrosis through machine learning

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the lack of reliable methods for predicting individual treatment response in chronic hepatitis B patients, as long-term antiviral therapy can reverse liver fibrosis in some individuals but not all.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This opinion review discusses the potential of machine learning to improve prediction of fibrosis reversal in chronic hepatitis B, focusing on clinical tools that are limited in capturing dynamic fibrosis processes.
analysis.methods: The authors review how machine learning can be applied to analyze images, integrate clinical and pathological data, and predict treatment response through serial measurements during antiviral therapy.
analysis.main_results: Machine learning has shown early but encouraging results in three areas: quantitative image analysis, multimodal integration of clinical and pathological data, and dynamic prediction of treatment response based on serial measurements.

It highlights the limitations of conventional clinical tools in capturing dynamic fibrosis processes and emphasizes the need for more robust models. title: Disruption of the NTCP–EGFR receptor complex as a strategy for selective inhibition of hepatitis B and D virus entry

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hepatitis B and D virus (HBV, HDV) enter hepatocytes through a coordinated process mediated by a receptor complex consisting of sodium taurocholate cotransporting polypeptide (NTCP), and host entry cofactors, including epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR).
analysis.study_design_and_population: Here, we established an in vitro assay to evaluate the NTCP–EGFR interaction and identified Oxy229, an oxysterol-based compound that disrupted this molecular interaction.
analysis.methods: Oxy229 selectively inhibited HBV and HDV infection to HepG2-NTCP cells and primary human hepatocytes.
analysis.main_results: Mechanistic analysis revealed that Oxy229 impaired the relocalization of HBV–NTCP complex from the plasma membrane to intracellular vesicles.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Notably, Oxy229 did not compromise the physiological functions of NTCP and EGFR, i.e., bile acid transporter and activation of downstream EGFR signaling pathways including Ras–MAPK and PI3K–Akt pathways, indicating selective inhibition of viral entry.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Compound derivative analysis identified Oxy283, which acquired dual inhibitory activity against both NTCP–EGFR interaction and NTCP multimerization, resulting in enhanced anti-HBV potency.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: These findings establish the functional significance of NTCP–receptor complex formation in the HBV/HDV entry and highlight this machinery as a potential target for antiviral intervention.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the mechanism of hepatitis B and D virus (HBV, HDV) entry into hepatocytes, focusing on the NTCP–EGFR receptor complex. The researchers developed an in vitro assay to evaluate this interaction and identified Oxy229, an oxysterol-based compound that disrupts the complex, selectively inhibiting HBV and HDV infection without affecting NTCP or EGFR physiological functions. Further analysis revealed that Oxy283, a derivative of Oxy229, has enhanced anti-HBV potency by targeting both NTCP–EGFR interaction and NTCP multimerization. These findings highlight the NTCP–receptor complex as a potential antiviral target. The study's evidence is strong, as it is based on direct mechanistic analysis and selective inhibition of viral entry. However, the findings are limited to in vitro settings and do not include clinical or in vivo data.

title: Nucleos(t)ide analogue discontinuation strategy to achieve the functional cure for chronic hepatitis B? A systematic review and meta-analysis.

analysis.scope_and_question: Functional cure rate is low during continuous nucleos(t)ide analog (NA) therapy, and therapy suspension has demonstrated interesting off-treatment responses.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A systematic review and meta-analysis to investigate how stable, HBsAg positive-virally suppressed patients would respond to drug discontinuation in terms of HBsAg clearance, clinical remission, virological relapses, alanine-aminotransferases (ALT) flares, and necessity of therapy reintroduction were performed.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: A total of 28 papers (4495 patients) were included in the analysis, with low risk of bias: HBsAg clearance rate at 24, 48 and 96 weeks were of 3%, 8% and 11% (95% IC 1-8%, 4-15%, 7-15%) respectively, with low to moderate heterogeneity (I2=58.4%%, 66.5%, 47.3%); according to the HBeAg status at NA introduction, in those HBeAg negative the HBsAg clearance rates were 3%, 8% and 10% at 24, 48 and 96 weeks, respectively, while in those HBeAg positive 2.3 and 3.4% at 24 and 48 weeks, respectively. Overall a higher HBsAg clearance rate (39% at 96 weeks, 95% CI=10-78%, I2=83.3%) was described in patients with HBsAg <100 UI/ml at discontinuation.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: These results showed an overall low rate of HBsAg clearance after NA discontinuation, except for the patients with low HBsAg titers at this time. Thus, NA discontinuation must be balanced in the single case for the risk of virological and clinical relapses.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Treatment reintroduction due to virological and clinical relapse rates were 21%, 12%, and 17% at 24, 48 and 96 weeks, respectively.

title: Semi-quantitative ultrasound scoring reveals hepatic structural recovery and immune modulation during tenofovir alafenamide therapy in chronic hepatitis B

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate the therapeutic response to tenofovir alafenamide fumarate (TAF) in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) using a semi-quantitative ultrasound (US) scoring system, and to investigate the correlation between sonographic changes and immune function restoration.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A total of 100 CHB patients who received TAF monotherapy (25 mg/day) for at least 24 months were retrospectively enrolled.
analysis.methods: A seven-parameter semi-quantitative US score, encompassing liver echogenicity, capsular contour, margin shape, vessel clarity, portal vein diameter (PVD), spleen thickness (ST), and splenic vein velocity (SVV), was calculated at baseline, 12 months, and 24 months. Concurrently, serum hepatitis B virus (HBV) deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA), alanine aminotransferase (ALT), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), peripheral T-cell subsets, including cluster of differentiation 3-positive (CD3 + ), CD4 + , CD8 + T cells, CD4+/CD8+ ratio, and natural killer (NK) cell activity were measured.
analysis.main_results: At 24 months, all patients achieved HBV DNA <20 IU/mL, with ALT and AST normalization rates of 92% and 95%, respectively. The comprehensive US score decreased significantly from 7.86 ± 1.73 at baseline to 3.37 ± 0.95 at 24 months (P < 0.001), with the most pronounced improvements observed in capsular smoothness and parenchymal homogeneity.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Correlations between US scores and biochemical/immune parameters were analyzed. The US score was positively correlated with ALT (r = 0.56) and AST (r = 0.47), and negatively correlated with the CD4 + /CD8 + ratio (r = −0.46) and NK cell activity (r = −0.38) (all P < 0.01).
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The strong correlations of US scores with biochemical and immune parameters support its utility as a non-invasive imaging biomarker for monitoring treatment efficacy and hepatic repair.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the therapeutic response to tenofovir alafenamide fumarate (TAF) in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) using a semi-quantitative ultrasound (US) scoring system. It aimed to assess the correlation between sonographic changes and immune function restoration. A total of 100 CHB patients on TAF monotherapy for at least 24 months were enrolled. The US score, which included seven parameters, was calculated at baseline, 12 months, and 24 months. Serum HBV DNA, ALT, AST, and immune parameters were also measured. At 24 months, all patients achieved HBV DNA <20 IU/mL, with ALT and AST normalization rates of 92% and 95%, respectively. The US score significantly decreased, indicating structural liver improvement. The US score correlated positively with ALT and AST and negatively with CD4+/CD8+ ratio and NK cell activity. These findings suggest that TAF not only suppresses viral replication and normalizes liver enzymes but also promotes measurable structural liver improvement. The strong correlations support the use of US as a non-invasive biomarker for monitoring treatment efficacy and hepatic repair. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the absence of reported limitations.

title: Testing for hepatitis C virus and hepatitis B virus/hepatitis D virus: Current scenarios and perspectives in Italy

analysis.scope_and_question: Liver disease accounts for approximately 4% of all deaths worldwide, and viral hepatitis affects more than 300 million people.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This expert-opinion review summarises the experience of tertiary-level Italian centres actively engaged in hospital-based testing for HCV, HBV, and HDV and identifies practical pathways to improve testing and linkage to care.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: In Italy, screening for hepatitis C virus (HCV) benefits from dedicated government funding, whereas testing for hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis D virus (HDV) is supported by recommendations from scientific societies but does not benefit from dedicated national public health programmes.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The World Health Organization aims to reduce new hepatitis infections by 90% and deaths by 65% by 2030 through vaccination and screening programs.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: This article presents proposals to improve the effectiveness of viral hepatitis management in Italy by: (1) Strengthening coordination between hospital units and integrating information systems between general practitioners and hospitals; (2) Implementing a centralised reporting system and a structured referral network to ensure that patients with positive test results receive appropriate therapies in a timely manner; (3) Providing the resources needed to increase testing in public addiction treatment services (Servizi per le Dipendenze) and prisons; (4) Promoting screening in high-risk populations, including vulnerable and older populations; and (5) Implementing a national awareness campaign on viral hepatitis.

analysis.summary_en: This review focuses on hepatitis B virus (HBV) in Italy, examining its impact and the current testing scenarios. It highlights that HBV testing is supported by scientific societies but lacks dedicated national public health programs compared to hepatitis C virus (HCV). The review identifies gaps in testing coverage, particularly in high-risk populations and specific healthcare settings. It proposes actionable strategies to enhance HBV management, including improved coordination between healthcare units, centralized reporting systems, increased testing in public services, targeted screening, and awareness campaigns. These measures aim to support Italy's efforts to control HBV within the next decade.

title: Selection, escape and the limits of inference in Middle Eastern hepatitis B virus genotype D: an analysis of 824 curated public sequences

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the public sequence archive of hepatitis B virus genotype D to determine if it could support inferences about selection and escape mechanisms in the Middle East. The background highlighted that HBV/D is prevalent in the region, but its sequence archive has not been rigorously tested for its ability to answer specific questions.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed 824 curated public sequences from ten Middle Eastern countries, including Iraq, to explore patterns of diversifying selection and escape substitutions. These sequences were sourced from GenBank and filtered based on collection date, surface-gene coverage, ambiguity, and within-country identity.
analysis.methods: The sequences were projected onto a genotype D reference, and a maximum-likelihood tree was inferred under GTR+Γ. Temporal signal was tested via root-to-tip regression, and ancestral country states were reconstructed using a discrete migration model, re-estimated on five country-balanced subsamples.
analysis.main_results: Of 4,398 retrieved records, 824 sequences from ten countries passed curation. Canonical resistance substitutions (rtL180M, rtM204V/I) and surface escape substitutions (sP120S/T, sS143L, sD144A/E/G, sG145R/A) were identified, with rtL180M and rtM204V/I being the most frequent (>2%). Twelve codons showed diversifying selection, but none were within classical escape positions.

This finding is novel as it challenges assumptions about immune-driven selection in HBV/D.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the understanding of immune-driven evolution in HBV/D and highlight the limitations of using surface-gene data for source attribution or transmission clustering. This has implications for improving surveillance and diagnostic strategies for genotype D hepatitis B.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The dataset lacks temporal signal and cannot be dated, and subgenotype assignment is limited due to sequence length and sampling design. Despite these limitations, the evidence is moderate, as the study provides a detailed analysis of curated sequences and their evolutionary patterns.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed 824 curated public sequences of hepatitis B virus genotype D from ten Middle Eastern countries to assess the archive's utility in understanding selection and escape mechanisms. The sequences were filtered and projected onto a genotype D reference, revealing canonical resistance and escape substitutions, with rtL180M and rtM204V/I being most frequent. The HBsAg antigenic loop showed no excess of diversifying selection, and escape positions lacked site-level signatures, suggesting escape occurs as rare events. The study highlights the limitations of surface-gene data for source attribution and transmission clustering, emphasizing the need for improved sampling and sequence length. The evidence is moderate, as the analysis is constrained by the dataset's characteristics rather than sample size.

title: Community-Based Detection of Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C, and Herpes Simplex Viruses in Northern Thailand

analysis.research_question_and_background: Blood-borne viral infections remain important public health concerns worldwide. The study aimed to provide updated community-based epidemiological data on HBV, HCV, and HSV in northern Thailand.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This cross-sectional study investigated HBsAg, anti-HCV antibodies, and HSV-1/HSV-2 DNA in a community-based population in northern Thailand. Serum samples from 779 participants were tested for HBsAg and anti-HCV, while whole-blood samples from 639 participants were tested for HSV-1 and HSV-2 DNA.
analysis.methods: Serum samples from 779 participants were tested for HBsAg and anti-HCV using rapid immunochromatographic assays, while whole-blood samples from 639 participants were tested for HSV-1 and HSV-2 DNA using real-time PCR. In the regression analysis, higher body weight was associated with lower odds of HBsAg detection (AOR = 0.955, 95% CI: 0.929–0.982; p = 0.001).
analysis.main_results: HBsAg and anti-HCV were detected in 3.0% (23/779) and 1.8% (14/779) of participants, respectively. HSV-1 and HSV-2 DNA were each detected in 0.5% (3/639) of whole-blood samples.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Because HSV DNA was detected infrequently and sequence confirmation was limited, the HSV findings should be interpreted with caution.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform surveillance and prevention strategies for HBV and HCV in northern Thailand. They also highlight the need for further studies involving larger populations, quantitative viral-load measurements, and longitudinal sampling.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited by the infrequency of HSV DNA detection and the lack of sequence confirmation. The study provides moderate confidence in its findings due to the cross-sectional design and the use of standard assays.

analysis.summary_en: This study conducted a cross-sectional survey in northern Thailand to assess the prevalence of HBV, HCV, and HSV infections in a community-based population. HBsAg and anti-HCV were detected in 3.0% and 1.8% of participants, respectively, while HSV-1 and HSV-2 DNA were found in 0.5% of whole-blood samples. The study highlights the importance of HBV and HCV as public health concerns and underscores the need for caution in interpreting HSV results due to low detection rates and limited sequence confirmation. The findings provide moderate confidence in the epidemiological data for HBV and HCV but emphasize the necessity for further research with larger populations and more detailed measurements.

title: Serum platelet-derived growth factor-BB as a noninvasive biomarker of significant liver fibrosis in patients with chronic hepatitis B: a cross-sectional study

analysis.research_question_and_background: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) is a major cause of progressive liver fibrosis (LF), cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma. This study aimed to evaluate serum platelet-derived growth factor-BB (PDGF-BB) as a noninvasive biomarker for detecting significant liver fibrosis in CHB patients.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This cross-sectional exploratory diagnostic accuracy study included 90 treatment-naive adults with CHB attending Tanta University Hospitals and Kafr El-Sheikh University Hospitals. A non-randomized convenience sampling approach was used to enroll participants.
analysis.methods: All participants underwent clinical evaluation; routine laboratory testing, including HBsAg, HBeAg, and serum HBV DNA; abdominal ultrasonography; serum PDGF-BB measurement by ELISA; and FibroScan examination. The optimal PDGF-BB cutoff was established based on the ROC curve derived from this cohort.
analysis.main_results: Among 90 patients, 69 (76.7%) had F0-F1 fibrosis and 21 (23.3%) had F2-F4 fibrosis. Median serum PDGF-BB was significantly increased in patients with F2-F4 than in those with F0-F1 fibrosis: 2500.8 (2028.25-2721.8) vs. 777.13 (479.21-1743.15) pg/mL, respectively (p < 0.001).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Serum PDGF-BB demonstrated good discrimination for VCTE-defined significant fibrosis in treatment-naive patients with CHB. Its negative predictive value of 95%, though prevalence-dependent, suggests potential utility as a triage or adjunctive biomarker.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that serum PDGF-BB could serve as a useful triage or adjunctive tool for identifying significant fibrosis in CHB patients, potentially reducing the need for invasive procedures.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: These findings are preliminary and require external validation before clinical implementation or substitution for elastography. The study used a non-randomized convenience sampling approach, which may limit generalizability.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study investigated serum platelet-derived growth factor-BB (PDGF-BB) as a noninvasive biomarker for detecting significant liver fibrosis in treatment-naive patients with chronic hepatitis B. The study included 90 participants from two university hospitals in Egypt. PDGF-BB levels were significantly higher in patients with F2-F4 fibrosis compared to those with F0-F1 fibrosis. The biomarker showed good discrimination with an AUC of 0.905, sensitivity of 85.7%, and specificity of 84.1%. However, the study's findings are preliminary and require external validation before clinical use. The results suggest that PDGF-BB could be a potential triage or adjunctive tool for assessing fibrosis in CHB patients, though its utility compared to existing markers like platelet count and INR remains to be confirmed.

title: Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver and antiviral response in chronic hepatitis B: A systematic review and meta-analysis

analysis.scope_and_question: The review aims to evaluate the impact of MAFLD on antiviral treatment responses and long-term clinical outcomes in patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB). The central question is whether MAFLD influences virological, biochemical, and clinical responses to antiviral therapy in CHB.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This systematic review and meta-analysis followed the PRISMA guidelines. The evidence base included studies from PubMed, the Cochrane Library, EMBASE, and Web of Science, published up to November 30, 2025. Subgroup analyses were conducted based on antiviral regimen and MAFLD diagnostic approach, and leave-one-out sensitivity analyses were performed to assess the robustness of findings.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: MAFLD was associated with lower virological and biochemical response rates, higher odds of hepatitis B surface antigen seroclearance at week 48, particularly among patients receiving nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy, and increased odds of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) despite antiviral therapy. However, no significant association was observed between MAFLD and hepatitis B e antigen seroclearance at any time-point.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Subgroup analyses suggested that antiviral regimen and MAFLD diagnostic approach partly explained the heterogeneity in the overall findings, particularly for hepatitis B virus DNA clearance and HCC. The evidence does not report on the specific mechanisms linking MAFLD to these outcomes or the impact of MAFLD on other clinical outcomes such as liver fibrosis progression.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The findings support the integration of metabolic risk assessment in the management of CHB and highlight the need for standardized definitions of MAFLD and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis investigates the association between metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) and antiviral treatment responses and long-term clinical outcomes in patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB). The review included 32 studies, with 20 evaluating treatment efficacy and 13 assessing clinical outcomes. MAFLD was linked to lower virological and biochemical response rates, higher odds of hepatitis B surface antigen seroclearance at week 48, and increased risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) despite antiviral therapy. However, no significant association was found with hepatitis B e antigen seroclearance. Subgroup analyses revealed heterogeneity in outcomes based on antiviral regimen and MAFLD diagnostic approach. The study underscores the importance of metabolic risk assessment in CHB management and calls for standardized definitions of MAFLD.

title: Prevalence of protective hepatitis B surface antibody levels and associated factors among women admitted for delivery at Kawempe National Referral Hospital, Uganda: A cross-sectional study

analysis.research_question_and_background: Mother-to-child transmission sustains the burden of hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection in sub-Saharan Africa, yet little is known about whether women giving birth in Uganda are protected.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We estimated the prevalence of protective hepatitis B surface antibody (anti-HBs) levels, described serological profiles and identified associated factors among women admitted for delivery at Kawempe National Referral Hospital, Kampala.
analysis.methods: In this cross-sectional study, 418 women were selected by systematic random sampling in 2024 and interviewed about socio-demographic characteristics, hepatitis B testing, vaccination and exposures.
analysis.main_results: Protective levels were found in 322 women (77.0%; 95% confidence interval [CI] 72.8–80.8): 50.6% of never-vaccinated women, 82.0% of those vaccinated before the current pregnancy only and 95.6% of those vaccinated during it.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: After adjustment, vaccination before the current pregnancy only (adjusted prevalence ratio 1.54; 95% CI 1.24–1.89) and during it (1.86; 95% CI 1.57–2.20) were associated with protection; no socio-demographic or behavioural factor was.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: One in five women reached delivery susceptible to HBV, largely because a negative test was not followed by vaccination.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Linking every negative antenatal test to vaccination could close much of this gap.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study conducted at Kawempe National Referral Hospital in Uganda aimed to assess the prevalence of protective hepatitis B surface antibody (anti-HBs) levels and associated factors among women giving birth. The study found that 77.0% of the 418 participants had protective levels, with higher rates among those vaccinated during the current pregnancy compared to those vaccinated before. After adjustment, vaccination during and before the current pregnancy was associated with protection, but no socio-demographic or behavioural factors were. The findings highlight the importance of ensuring vaccination following negative antenatal tests to reduce susceptibility to HBV. The study's evidence is moderate, as it is based on an abstract-only report and does not provide detailed statistical or methodological information.

title: Longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis with concurrent acute sensorimotor polyneuropathy secondary to hepatitis B virus reactivation: a case report

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) reactivation is a recognised complication of immunosuppressive therapy, and neurological complications from HBV reactivation are rare, particularly concurrent involvement of the central and peripheral nervous systems.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We report a case of longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis (LETM) with concurrent acute sensorimotor polyneuropathy following HBV reactivation after rituximab containing chemotherapy for diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.
analysis.methods: The patient received rituximab based chemotherapy, with entecavir prescribed as antiviral prophylaxis because of previous HBV exposure. Entecavir was discontinued one month following cessation of chemotherapy, and six months later, he developed virologically confirmed HBV reactivation.
analysis.main_results: Neurological examination demonstrated bilateral lower limb weakness, areflexia, and a thoracic sensory level with impaired vibration and proprioception. Magnetic resonance imaging and nerve conduction studies demonstrated a sensorimotor polyneuropathy with axonal abnormalities and features suggestive of demyelination.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: HBV reactivation may rarely present with concurrent LETM and acute sensorimotor polyneuropathy. In patients presenting with acute myeloneuropathy following rituximab containing chemotherapy, particularly after premature discontinuation of antiviral prophylaxis, HBV reactivation should be considered in the differential diagnosis.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Early recognition and combined antiviral and immunomodulatory therapy may be associated with favourable neurological outcomes.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report specific design limitations or bias.

analysis.summary_en: This case report describes a patient with HBV reactivation presenting with LETM and acute sensorimotor polyneuropathy following rituximab-based chemotherapy. Early recognition and combined antiviral and immunomodulatory therapy may lead to favourable neurological outcomes.

title: Artificial intelligence-driven risk estimation, early detection, diagnostic characterisation and prognosis in hepatitis b-related hepatocellular carcinoma

analysis.scope_and_question: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains the leading global antecedent of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), yet the surveillance framework on which early detection depends is constrained at both of its load-bearing points: The modest sensitivity of biannual ultrasonography for early-stage tumours, and the bounded discrimination of risk scores that compress a nonlinear, time-evolving process into a small set of additively weighted covariates.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: Artificial intelligence (AI) has been advanced as a corrective, but the term is applied loosely and the supporting evidence is drawn from heterogeneous populations and from clinical tasks that are frequently conflated. We state what is and is not counted as AI, describe the search strategy and selection principles, and categorise every cited study according to whether its evidence is HBV-specific, mixed-aetiology, hepatitis C virus-derived, drawn from general HCC populations, or confined to recurrence and prognosis.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Where machine-learning models built on routine clinical variables have been compared with established scores within a single validation cohort, they have discriminated more accurately. These findings rest on a literature that is predominantly retrospective and single-centre, in which external validation is the exception, calibration is reported inconsistently, explainability is uneven, and meta-analysts repeatedly judge the underlying studies to be at high risk of bias.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Evidence drawn specifically from hepatitis B cohorts remains a minority of the published work, and no study has demonstrated that an AI-guided strategy improves stage at diagnosis or survival.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Prospective multicentre validation, transparent calibration, adherence to TRIPOD+AI and PROBAST+AI, and deliberate inclusion of African and South Asian populations are therefore prerequisites rather than refinements.

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in addressing challenges in the surveillance, detection, and management of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) associated with hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection. It highlights the limitations of current methods, such as the modest sensitivity of ultrasonography and the bounded discrimination of risk scores. The review categorises studies based on their focus on HBV-specific evidence, mixed aetiologies, or other related viruses like hepatitis C. It finds that AI models, when compared to traditional scores within single validation cohorts, show improved discrimination. However, the evidence is largely retrospective and single-centre, with limited external validation and inconsistent calibration. The review concludes that AI strategies require prospective multicentre validation, transparent calibration, and inclusion of underrepresented populations to be effective in improving outcomes for HBV-related HCC.

title: Time-Resolved Proteomic Analysis of Hepatitis B Virus Infection

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is a major cause of chronic liver disease and hepatocellular carcinoma, yet its impact on host proteome dynamics during early infection remains poorly defined.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Here, we performed time-resolved label-free quantitative (LFQ) proteomics to characterize the host response to HBV infection in human HepG2 hepatoma cells.
analysis.methods: Across five time points spanning the first 3 weeks of infection, we quantified 5365 unique proteins, including two HBV proteins (C/preC-derived and S), revealing subtle yet coordinated changes in the hepatocellular proteome.
analysis.main_results: Early infection was characterized by selective alterations in cytoskeletal organization, extracellular matrix components, and focal adhesion pathways, alongside enrichment of complement-associated proteins.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Notably, we identified a transient, specific increase in the abundance of complement component C5 without a corresponding change in C3, indicating differential regulation of complement pathway members during infection.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings define a temporally resolved proteomic landscape of HBV–host interactions and uncover previously underappreciated complement dynamics consistent with a selective and restrained host response.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Together, our results provide a framework for mechanistic studies of early viral infection and host adaptation.

analysis.summary_en: This study used time-resolved label-free quantitative proteomics to investigate the host response to hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection in human HepG2 hepatoma cells. The research aimed to better understand the proteomic changes during early HBV infection, which is a major cause of chronic liver disease and hepatocellular carcinoma. The study quantified 5365 unique proteins across five time points, revealing coordinated changes in the hepatocellular proteome, including alterations in cytoskeletal organization, extracellular matrix components, and focal adhesion pathways. A notable finding was a transient increase in complement component C5 without a corresponding change in C3, suggesting differential regulation of complement pathway members. These results offer a detailed proteomic landscape of HBV-host interactions and highlight previously underappreciated complement dynamics. The study provides a framework for understanding early viral infection mechanisms and host adaptation. However, the findings are limited to in vitro models and do not account for in vivo complexities, which may affect their generalizability.

title: Seroprevalence of hepatitis B and hepatitis C and its trends in India: a systematic review and meta-analysis

analysis.scope_and_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to synthesize HBV and HCV seroprevalence in India from available evidence and identify variations across key subpopulations.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A systematic search was conducted on PubMed, Embase, and Scopus for studies published from January 1999 to September 2024 reporting HBV and/or HCV seroprevalence in India. Following PRISMA guidelines, 87 studies (61 on HBV, 69 on HCV) were included. Given substantial heterogeneity across studies, pooled seroprevalence was estimated using a random-effects model.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The pooled seroprevalence was 3.0% [95% CI 2.0–4.0%] for HBV (HBsAg + ) ( n = 693,879 participants) and 4.0% [95% CI: 2.0–7.0%] for anti-HCV antibody ( n = 1,079,706 participants). HBV prevalence ranged from approximately 1.0% among blood donors to higher levels in community-based settings (7.0%) and high-risk populations (4.0%). Geographically, HBV prevalence was highest in Northern (3.0%) and Western (3.0%) India. For HCV, prevalence was markedly higher among high-risk populations (11.0%).
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Considerable heterogeneity was observed across studies ( I 2 > 99%), reflecting differences in study populations, geographic regions, and study settings. These findings indicate considerable heterogeneity in the epidemiology of viral hepatitis across populations in India.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Scaling up community-based screening, decentralizing molecular testing, and improving linkage-to-care are essential to strengthen India’s National Viral Hepatitis Control Programme (NVHCP) and to achieve the WHO 2030 Viral Hepatitis elimination targets.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis assessed the seroprevalence of hepatitis B (HBV) and hepatitis C (HCV) in India, highlighting significant variability across populations, geographic regions, and study designs. The pooled HBV seroprevalence was 3.0% (95% CI 2.0–4.0%) among 693,879 participants, while HCV prevalence was 4.0% (95% CI 2.0–7.0%) among 1,079,706 participants. Subgroup analyses revealed higher HBV prevalence in community-based and high-risk populations, with Northern and Western India showing the highest rates. HCV prevalence was notably higher in high-risk groups. The study underscores the need for targeted interventions, including community-based screening and improved linkage-to-care, to address the persistent burden of viral hepatitis in India and meet global elimination targets.

title: A composite lymph node-targeting nanoadjuvant NA@DCM integrates TLR9 and mitochondrial metabolic reprogramming for enhanced hepatitis B vaccination

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a major global public health concern. Although hepatitis B subunit vaccines are safe and effective, improved adjuvants may further enhance their immunogenicity.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We developed NA@DCM, an aluminum-based composite nanoadjuvant in which DSPE-PEG 2000 nanomicelles incorporating a covalently conjugated DSPE-PEG–CpG 1018 (DC) conjugate are interfacially assembled with nano-aluminum (NA). analysis.methods: Compared with its individual components and their physical mixture, NA@DCM increased antigen-specific IgG titers, the IgG2c/IgG1 ratio, IFN-γ + /TNF-α + / IL-2 + /IL-4 + CD4 + and CD8 + T cells, and germinal center responses, and matched an AS04-like reference formulation in total IgG.

analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Oligomycin A inhibition of ATP synthase attenuated bioenergetic responses and CD69/CD86 upregulation in human Namalwa and primary murine B cells, indicating mitochondrial ATP synthesis is required for NA@DCM-induced B-cell activation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: NA@DCM showed favorable hemocompatibility in vitro and no overt acute toxicity in vivo ; repeated immunization induced early cytokine responses and local infiltration without detectable hepatic or renal abnormalities.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Collectively, NA@DCM integrates lymph node-targeted delivery, TLR9-associated signaling, and mitochondrial bioenergetic modulation, supporting further preclinical development as a hepatitis B vaccine adjuvant.

Results showed that NA@DCM significantly increased antigen-specific IgG titers, the IgG2c/IgG1 ratio, and T-cell responses compared to its individual components. Mechanistically, the nanoadjuvant enhanced TLR9–NF-κB signaling and mitochondrial function, with evidence that mitochondrial ATP synthesis is essential for B-cell activation. The study also demonstrated favorable hemocompatibility and safety profiles in vitro and in vivo. These findings suggest that NA@DCM could be a promising candidate for improving hepatitis B vaccine efficacy. However, the study is limited to murine models, and further research is needed to confirm its effectiveness in humans.

title: Investigation of a rise in newly acquired hepatitis B in a metropolitan setting: insights from whole genome sequencing

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate a rise in newly acquired hepatitis B cases in metropolitan Perth to understand the potential outbreak and transmission dynamics.
analysis.study_design_and_population: An outbreak investigation was conducted in metropolitan Perth between 1 August 2023 and 31 July 2024, including 20 newly acquired cases and three additional cases for further analysis.
analysis.methods: Epidemiological analyses of demographics, disease onset, and risk factors were combined with laboratory investigations, including whole genome sequencing (WGS) for genotyping and phylogenetic analysis.
analysis.main_results: Most cases were aged over 30 years (n = 18, 78%) and reported casual unprotected sex (n = 17, 74%); some were born overseas (n = 8, 33%) or used intravenous drugs (n = 7, 30%). Of the 20 sequenced cases, 12 were locally acquired sub-genotype A2 HBV.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study identified three sub-genotype A2 clusters and one sub-genotype B3 cluster, highlighting the role of WGS in complementing traditional epidemiological methods to better understand transmission patterns.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that the increase in sub-genotype A2 cases may be due to multiple introductions of HBV strains into Perth, with limited local transmission, informing targeted public health interventions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Genetic diversity within individual patient samples complicated relatedness analyses, and the study's results were limited by the small sample size and the lack of clear epidemiological links.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated a rise in newly acquired hepatitis B cases in metropolitan Perth between 1 August 2023 and 31 July 2024. The outbreak was analyzed using epidemiological data and whole genome sequencing (WGS) to determine transmission dynamics. Most cases were over 30 years old and reported casual unprotected sex, with some born overseas or using intravenous drugs. Of the 20 sequenced cases, 12 were sub-genotype A2 HBV, and three clusters of this genotype were identified, along with one sub-genotype B3 cluster. The study suggests that the increase in cases may result from multiple introductions of HBV strains into Perth, with limited local transmission. While WGS provided insights, within-host sequence heterogeneity complicated relatedness analyses. The findings have implications for public health surveillance and intervention strategies in the region.

title: Hepatitis B Reactivation and Infection in People with HIV on Tenofovir-Sparing Antiretroviral Therapy

analysis.research_question_and_background: As more people with HIV (PWH) transition to tenofovir (TXF)-sparing antiretroviral therapy (ART), the risk of hepatitis B virus (HBV) reactivation (HBVr) and new infection (HBVi) is a concern.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We conducted a retrospective study of 5,776 PWH in the Centers for AIDS Research Network of Integrated Clinical Systems cohort without active HBV infection with ≥1 TXF-sparing ART regimen prescribed after 5/1/2014 and examined episodes of HBVi/r defined as new HBV surface antigen (HBsAg) positivity or HBV viremia.
analysis.methods: We calculated rate of HBVi/r over total time on TXF-sparing ART per 10,000 person-years.
analysis.main_results: We identified 17 cases of HBVi/r over a median 5.3 years of follow up.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The rate of HBVi was 3.9 per 10,000 person-years, and rate of HBVr was 6.0 per 10,000 person-years, with possible higher risk for those who were HBV surface antibody (HBsAb) negative at cohort entry and among those not on ART with no anti-HBV activity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: HBVi/r on TXF-sparing ART was rare in this U.S. cohort, but providers should check complete HBV serologies, offer initial or additional vaccination as needed, and monitor for potential HBVi/r.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report limitations or evidence strength for this study.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the risk of hepatitis B virus (HBV) reactivation (HBVr) and new infection (HBVi) in people with HIV (PWH) transitioning to tenofovir-sparing antiretroviral therapy (ART). The study found that HBVi/r occurred at a low rate, with 17 cases identified over a median of 5.3 years of follow-up. The risk was higher for individuals who were HBV surface antibody (HBsAb) negative at cohort entry and those not on ART with no anti-HBV activity. analysis.summary_en: This study characterizes needlestick injuries (NSIs) and post-exposure practices among healthcare workers (HCWs) in private hospitals in Alexandria, Egypt. It found that most NSIs occurred among female HCWs, with nurses being the most affected group. Syringes were involved in 65.1% of NSIs, and sudden patient movement was the most frequently reported contributing factor. The study also noted that 79.8% of HCWs with documented IPC training status had no prior training, and 16.0% were unvaccinated against hepatitis B. Post-exposure actions were not documented in 30.8% of records, and only 29.6% underwent documented post-exposure testing for hepatitis C virus, hepatitis B, and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). These findings highlight gaps in IPC training, hepatitis B vaccination, and post-exposure management, underscoring the need for standardized reporting and improved occupational safety practices. The study's reliance on retrospective records limits its evidence strength, which is assessed as moderate.
